A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Flash-GRPO. All 21 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-model alignment experiments, including VBench results, component ablations, reward curves and qualitative comparisons in Section 5 and Appendices A, B and D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–2, training and evaluation curves, and supplementary qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The single-step ODE/SDE procedure, iso-temporal grouping and temporal gradient rectification are unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1 in Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DanceGRPO prompt dataset and VBench coverage for video alignment. Visual-quality, motion-quality and qualitative prompt-following scenarios, including Appendix D, are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CogVideoX-2B, Hunyuan-Video, vanilla Wan2.1, Flow-GRPO-Fast1 and Flow-GRPO. Comparator membership in the reward-curve, ablation and appendix comparisons also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the 300-prompt evaluation split, 1.3B/14B models, 20/12 training sampling steps, 50 inference steps and reward aggregation. The 350-GPU-hour comparison and KL-controlled experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same component ablations. The KL comparisons, gradient-norm analysis and rectification analysis in Figures 4, 7 and 8, together with Appendix D's qualitative cases, are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-score tables and plotted trajectories. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, curves and qualitative examples match throughout. For example, Flash-GRPO's Table 1 aesthetic score remains 66.43, and its full-method evaluation reward in Table 2 remains 5.42. Appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain Equations 1–11, including the GRPO/SDE formulation, grouping definition, derivation of the time-dependent gradient factor and rectified loss. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about stable single-step alignment, reduced computational cost and performance relative to full-trajectory training on 1.3B–14B video models.

C2.justification: The explanations involving timestep-confounded advantages and gradient-scale imbalance are unchanged, as are interpretations of stability and quality results. The low-computational-budget qualifications remain, with no new limitations or applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including CFG 4.5, clipping ratio 0.001, sampling schedules, Appendix C's pseudocode and Appendix D's exact prompts. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2's G2RPO citation changes from Guo et al.'s G2RPO-A: Guided Group Relative Policy Optimization with Adaptive Guidance (v1 reference 4) to Zhou et al.'s Fine-grained GRPO for Precise Preference Alignment in Flow Models (v3 reference 32). This replaces one cited work; the surrounding positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page equal-contribution asterisk is removed from Zeyue Xue. The arXiv version/date and citation numbering are updated, while the substantive prose, section order and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The bibliography reflows across pages 11–12, moving the Latte entry from page 12 to page 11. Figures 1–12, Tables 1–2, Algorithm 1 and the appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The method, mathematical argument, experimental evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged, including all appendix material. The isolated citation replacement, author-contribution marker edit and bibliography reflow do not establish a meaningful overall gain or loss in scientific support or clarity.
